name: Dettifoss to Ásbyrgi canyon trek
region: Jökulsárgljúfur, Vatnajökull National Park, North Iceland
why: Two days down the west side of the Jökulsá canyon, from the thundering Dettifoss past basalt column rosettes and red craters to the horseshoe cliffs of Ásbyrgi.
book: Camping only at the park campsites of Dettifoss, Vesturdalur and Ásbyrgi: no huts on the route. Arrange a car or transfer to Dettifoss west and back from Ásbyrgi. Ask at the Gljúfrastofa visitor centre in Ásbyrgi about trail conditions.
water: No streams or springs between Vesturdalur and Ásbyrgi: carry all you need there. The Stallá is shallow and cold, but you must wade it.
dangers: Long sections on the canyon rim with high drops: keep back from the edge in wind.
The Hafragil lowland descent and the rope at Tófugjá are no place for a heavy pack: take the rim trail.
Cold wade of the Stallá, a spring river: sandals for the crossing.
turnaround: Fog or gale on the first day: stop at Hólmatungur, where a road reaches the trail.

points.name: Dettifoss
points.note: The west-bank viewpoint over the falls in grey glacier water. The trail heads north along the rim past the Hafragil ravine.

points.name: Hólmatungur
points.note: Green spring-fed river meadows in the canyon, about 11.5 km from Dettifoss; a road ends here.

points.name: Vesturdalur campsite
points.note: After the Stallá ford and the twin rock Karl og Kerling, the park campsite in a grassy valley, about 8 km from Hólmatungur.

points.name: Hljóðaklettar
points.note: The 'echo rocks': old volcanic plugs with basalt columns in rosettes and curls by the river. A short loop leads through them.

points.name: Ásbyrgi
points.note: Along the rim of the horseshoe canyon of Ásbyrgi and down by Tófugjá to the Gljúfrastofa visitor centre and campsite.
